goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration string-interpolates host values into `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` with no quoting, so a value containing `'` breaks the migration or injects SQL; should use quote/bind params

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration loops through `records.each do |h|` and runs `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The host value `h` comes from the `site_settings` table (`embeddable_hosts`), and is directly interpolated into SQL inside single quotes with no escaping/quoting. If `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the SQL will break, and it also enables SQL injection during migration if an attacker/admin-controlled setting contains crafted input. Using `quote(h)`/bind params would avoid this.

store.js.es6 `_ids` branch unconditionally deletes `obj[k]` and replaces it with `_lookupSubType` results, so when the sideloaded collection is absent the result is an array of undefined and the original id list is lost; also `obj[k].map` throws if the value is null and `hydrated || []` is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new `_ids` handling does `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that `obj[k]` is an array; if the server sends `*_ids: null` (or omits it / sends non-array), this will throw at runtime. Additionally, it always `delete obj[k]` and sets `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` to the mapped lookup results even when `_lookupSubType` can’t find sideloaded records, producing an array of `undefined` and losing the original id list. Finally, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead code because `map` always returns an array (truthy), even when empty.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHost` format regex allows a `:port` suffix but `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host` which never includes the port, so a stored `example.com:8080` is valid yet can never match

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` permits saving hosts with a `:port` suffix via the validation regex (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and the `before_validation` hook strips scheme and path but does not strip the port. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(...)` and compares using `uri.host`, which never includes the port, against `embeddable_hosts.host` (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`). Therefore a saved record like `example.com:8080` is valid but will never match any referer, making it effectively unusable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable-host.js.es6 component sets `host.category` from `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)` after save, so when no category was chosen the client sets `category` to undefined and the row shows blank until reload, despite the server falling back to uncategorized

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6#save`, the client always does `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and after a successful save forcibly sets `host.category` from `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`. On the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` explicitly falls back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when `category_id` is blank. If the user saves without choosing a category (i.e., `categoryId` remains `null`/blank on the client), the server will persist uncategorized, but the client will set `host.category` using `findById(null)` (undefined), overriding any correct server-side/defaulted category and causing the category badge to appear blank until reload/rehydration. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff (client uses local `categoryId` rather than the server-returned value).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `PUT customize/embedding` route and `saveChanges` calling `update({})` form a dead endpoint: `update` persists nothing and just re-renders, returning success without doing anything, and the template never triggers `saveChanges`

adjudication.rationale: In `config/routes.rb` a `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` route is added. The corresponding `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` method does not read params or mutate any persisted state; it just re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit that PUT endpoint with an empty payload. However, the `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` template contains only host list rendering and an `addHost` button; there is no button/action wired to `saveChanges`. All persistence in the UI happens via `embeddable-host` component calling `host.save(props)` / `destroyRecord()` against `/admin/embeddable_hosts`. So the PUT endpoint and `saveChanges` action are effectively dead and currently return success while persisting nothing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` now hit the DB on every embed request (previously an in-memory site setting) and the `embeddable_hosts` table has no index on `host`; with `lower(host)` in the predicate a functional index or lowercased storage is needed

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes embed host checks from an in-memory SiteSetting list to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `record_for_host`. This is called from `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, so it will perform a DB query on each such check. The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` adds no index on `host`, and because the predicate wraps the column in `lower(host)`, even a plain index on `host` would typically not be used without a functional index (or normalized lowercased storage). This is a concrete performance defect introduced by the diff.

rest.js.es6 adapter `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore, so any future multi-underscore admin model name would miss the `/admin/` base path

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `basePath(store, type)` now checks `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1` with `ADMIN_MODELS = ['plugin','site-customization','embeddable-host']`. All admin model names referenced here have at most one underscore in their likely Ember type form (`site_customization`, `embeddable_host`), so replacing only the first underscore is sufficient for the models in this change. The proposed issue only arises for hypothetical future admin models with multiple underscores, which is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.
